description: OJP, the Open API for distributed Journey Planning, is the European technical specification CEN/TS 17118:2017 for linking separate journey planners so that a trip can be planned across regions and countries. The GitHub repository maintained by VDV, the German association of transport companies, holds the XML Schema, examples and generated documentation tables. Coverage: services for place information, stop events (departure and arrival boards), trip search, trip information, fares, trip changes and refinement, leg availability and line information, plus exchange points and multipoint trips for systems that talk to each other. OJP belongs to the Transmodel family with NeTEx, SIRI and OpRa and reuses elements of DATEX II; it is referenced by the EU delegated regulation on multimodal travel information services. Format and access: XSD files and XML examples downloadable from GitHub, with releases 1.0 (the version in the CEN document), 1.0.1 and 2.0; documentation tables on vdvde.github.io; the formal standard document is sold by CEN. Licence: no licence file in the repository (not stated); the CEN document is paid. Caveats: this is an interface specification without data, implementations differ by country, and the GitHub site pages returned 403 so the wiki of implementations was not read. Simulation uses: a common request and response model for coupling regional journey planners in digital twins and network flow studies of cross-border public transport. Related records: Transmodel, NeTEx and SIRI (data-transmodel-netex-siri-standards) and DATEX II (data-datex-ii-standard).
